title: Festival Wheel
description: A 12-month calendar wheel of South Asian festivals. A year slider (1990 to 2060) moves dates that are computed from the Moon's phases, showing that solar festivals stay fixed, lunisolar festivals shift within a season, and Islamic festivals move about 11 days earlier every Gregorian year.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Festivals
Calendars
Lunar and solar years
World religions
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Explain why festivals on a solar calendar keep the same Gregorian date each year.
Explain why lunisolar festivals such as Diwali and Holi move by up to a month but stay in the same season.
Explain why Islamic festivals such as Eid al-Fitr move about 11 days earlier each Gregorian year and circle the whole year in about 33 years.
prerequisites: Knowing that a year is one trip of the Earth around the Sun
Knowing that the Moon goes through phases (new moon to full moon and back) about once a month
keyQuestions: Why does Eid come about 11 days earlier every year?
Why do Diwali and Holi move around but never leave their season?
Which festivals keep the same date every year, and why?
misconceptions: All festivals that follow the moon move the same way.
Eid moves because people choose a new date each year.
A computed calendar date is always the date a community actually celebrates.
controls: Color by calendar type or faith menu
Show Islamic dates from the past 4 years checkbox
Click or tap a festival dot or label
dataSources: Jean Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms (2nd ed., 1998), chapter 49, phases of the Moon (algorithm used to compute new and full moons)

Government of India, Department of Personnel and Training, holidays for central government offices in 2026 (used to check computed dates): https://www.gconnect.in/news/holidays-to-be-observed-in-central-government-offices-during-the-year-2026.html
